_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: idx 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (idx 0 bilingual cover 'SET-2 / Q.P. Code 55/3/2', idx 1 Hindi General Instructions, idx 2 English General Instructions, idx 3/5/7/9 Hindi, idx 11 blank folio 12). The booklet is HINDI-FIRST: each Hindi page is immediately followed by its English twin covering exactly the same questions, so no block spills across a language boundary. Verified by cropping the top 320 px of every odd page into one strip and reading it at full size — idx 3 opens 'खण्ड - क' with Hindi Q1 and Q2(a), idx 5 opens Hindi Q7 and Q8, idx 7 opens the Hindi OR-alternative (a)/(b) of Q11, idx 9 opens Hindi 'III.' — so NO English overflow at the top of ANY odd page. idx 11 read at full size is genuinely blank (a lone asterisk, the QR block and the '.55/3/2  257 B  12' footer; no scanner show-through, mirrored or otherwise). The QP PDF is a pure image scan — the paper index records textChars=0 — so every reading of the paper here is by vision. PRINTED GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS AGREE with the term2_sci table: (i) 12 questions, (ii) three sections A/B/C, (iii) Section A Q1-3 @2, (iv) Section B Q4-11 @3, (v) Section C Q12 a case study of 5 marks; 6+24+5 = 35, matching the cover's 'Maximum Marks : 35' and the marking scheme's own 'A full scale of marks ___35___'. NOTE this paper prints SEVEN general instructions, with (vi) the internal-choice line and (vii) the log-tables line — the SCIENCE_ADDENDUM records that the 2022 CHEMISTRY papers print only six and put log tables at (vi), so the 'term2_sci papers print no internal-choice line at all' warning is a CHEMISTRY fact, not a pattern fact; this Physics paper does print one. It still gives NO COUNT ('internal choice has been provided in some of the questions'), so the roster was built the way the addendum prescribes. DECIMAL POINTS: this paper prints ORDINARY FULL STOPS throughout, confirmed at 3x magnification (6.5, 2.14, 1.33, 4.1 MeV, 41.1 degrees, 1.2, 1.2 cm, 3.0 cm, 1.25 cm, and the constants 6.63 / 8.854 / 1.675 / 1.673 / 6.023 / 1.38 on the instructions page). Its own MARKING SCHEME prints RAISED dots (4·1, 1·6, 1·673, 2·88) — the documented paper-disagrees-with-its-own-scheme case; the PAPER is what is transcribed. INTERNAL CHOICE: THREE (Q3, Q6, Q11), established two independent ways — a printed 'OR' on the English page with the matching 'अथवा' on its Hindi twin, AND exactly three bare 'OR' lines of their own in the marking scheme's text layer (no OR-inside-an-answer false positives). Primary branches sum to 35. ⚠ THIS PAPER HAS FIVE MCQs — Section C's case study is five 1-mark MCQs with four printed options each, marked '1 × 5 = 5' on the paper, and the marking scheme keys all five verbatim in its own SECTION—C table. See the _flag on Q12I. VOID SCAN: the marking scheme's text layer IS readable here (13,020 characters across our block) so the scan was programmatic as well as visual. All 8 rendered ms pages were read at full size, AND the text of PDF pages 8..15 (0-based) was scanned with a file-authored probe carrying a self-test that first proved it fires on six known-bad fixtures (CBSE's real void wordings, including the keyless and medium-scoped shapes) and stays silent on three known-good ones. ZERO question-level voids and ZERO medium-scoped clauses. The single regex hit is the boilerplate evaluator instruction 10 ('Please do not hesitate to award full marks if the answer deserves it'), which is not a void. ⚠ PAGE-RANGE NOTE for whoever reads this scheme next: `_papers.physics.json` records msPages {from: 8, to: 15} and those numbers are 0-BASED. Reading them as 1-based pulls in 55/3/1's page 8 and drops 55/3/2's, which is exactly the merged-scheme slip SCIENCE_ADDENDUM warns attaches a void to the wrong question. I made that error first; every page of the correct block (pdf 8..15) carries a '042_55/3/2_Physics # Page-N' footer, 10 occurrences of 55/3/2 and ZERO of either sibling, which is how it was settled. The rendered ms/p00..p07 are the CORRECT block.

questions.subtopic: Refraction and Reflection of Plane Waves
questions._flag: FILING NOTE, not a defect. This question sits between two chapters and was filed on the closest fit rather than flagged as a gap. What it actually tests is which of wavelength, frequency and speed change when light crosses into a denser medium — the marking scheme's answer is 'No change in wavelength' and \(c = 3 \times 10^8\) m/s for the reflected light, and \(\lambda' = \lambda/\mu = 451.1\) nm, \(v = c/\mu = 2.26 \times 10^8\) m/s, \(\nu = 5 \times 10^{14}\) Hz unchanged for the refracted light. That frequency-is-conserved-while-wavelength-and-speed-scale result is derived in NCERT Ch.10 §10.2 (refraction and reflection of plane waves by Huygens' principle), hence Wave Optics. The rival home is Ray Optics / 'Refraction and Total Internal Reflection', which teaches the bending of rays by Snell's law rather than what happens to the wave's own parameters. No subtopic invented.

Read off MY OWN page idx 8, not copied from the opener: a point marked by a filled dot and labelled O sits at the left, with a horizontal DASHED line running right from it, through the circle, to the circle's centre — the centre is a filled dot labelled C, and a SOLID segment continues from C to the circle's right edge, labelled r. questions.context: A compound microscope consists of two converging lenses. One of them, of smaller aperture and smaller focal length is called objective and the other of slightly larger aperture and slightly larger focal length is called eye-piece. Both the lenses are fitted in a tube with an arrangement to vary the distance between them. A tiny object is placed in front of the objective at a distance slightly greater than its focal length. The objective produces the image of the object which acts as an object for the eye-piece. The eye piece, in turn produces the final magnified image.
